transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-30
Start: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery, Sofia, Marcus, Lena, Ethan, Riley, Priya

Summary: quick internal incident review after canary broke KV cache and caused elevated p95s and retries. Note: auto-transcript, some words garbled.

00:00 Avery: yeah okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining, we'll run through the incident timeline then, um, decisions for the launch gate. Marcus can you start with the timeline?
00:14 Marcus: sure. so around 03:10 UTC on Thursday we started the canary for the v2 runtime - small percentage, 5%. within ~12 minutes we saw the per-host KV cache miss rate spike, which then correlates with a CPU bump on the shard leader, and that cascaded into client-side retries, i'm seeing retry storms, p95 climbed from 220ms to 1.2s on affected routes.
00:37 Sofia: and just to add, the autoscaler engaged, which is right, but because eviction was synchronous it triggered a flurry of writes, so the evictions actually amplified latency rather than smoothing.
00:52 Marcus: yeah and there's a subtle interaction with the new eviction policy we shipped - the threshold was too low for the heavy-tail prefix workload we were seeing. the canary had a slightly different traffic shape than our tests.
01:08 Ethan: i think what's important is that the telemetry we had wasn't surface enough to correlate eviction churn to client retries quickly; we got paged but it took us 20 minutes to pinpoint.
01:22 Riley: right, and ops didn't have a rollback runbook for that canary path specifically, so the initial mitigation was toggling traffic which took a while.
01:32 Priya: QA reported that our stress tests didn't simulate the long-tail sequence lengths; we used uniform distributions which masked the eviction behavior.
01:45 Avery: ok, thanks. let's talk mitigations — short term what did we do? Marcus?
01:52 Marcus: short term we removed the canary percentage and bumped the cache capacity on the cluster. that brought p95 back down to baseline over ~25 minutes. we also temporarily disabled the synchronous eviction path for the shard leader which reduced write amplification.
02:12 Sofia: for the next rollout we want to gate on two metrics: per-shard eviction rate and per-route retry rate hitting >5% within a 10-minute window triggers an automatic pause. that should let autoscaler do its job without us knee-jerking.
02:29 Lena: i noted a communications gap — we need a clear channel and playbook so that product, engineering and on-call are aligned on thresholds and who toggles what.
02:40 Marcus: agreed. i'll own the runbook draft.
02:45 Avery: great. any thoughts on root cause — is this primarily a config mismatch or do we need runtime changes?
02:52 Ethan: my hypothesis is config + instrumentation. the eviction policy is aggressive by default; runtime should expose per-prefix eviction weights and per-request metadata so we can prioritize hot prefixes. a longer-term fix is smarter eviction, but that may take a sprint.
03:15 Sofia: and we should also look at the kernel path timings — the kernel selection for small sequence lengths seems suboptimal for this workload; might be contributing to CPU spikes.
03:28 Marcus: yep, compiling that with the perf team.
03:32 Priya: for QA i'll add a test that injects long sequence prefixes and measures eviction churn; we'll run that in our nightly integration and before canary.
03:43 Avery: okay items: Marcus runbook, Ethan instrumentation, Priya tests, Riley rollback doc — thanks.
03:51 Riley: one more quick note, we should keep the canary percent lower and use staged ramping, like 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, with 30m dwell per stage for this release.
04:06 Sofia: yes and add synthetic replay that mimics tail heavy sessions in staging; that will catch both eviction and kernel issues.
04:15 Marcus: do we want to change autoscaler config in the short term? there's a risk if we increase headroom we'll just raise cost.
04:23 Avery: decision — don't change autoscaler for now, focus on eviction thresholds and better telemetry. we'll revisit if we see repeat issues in the staging replay.
04:33 Lena: on communications, i'll make a checklist and a confluence page "Launch Readiness: eviction & canary playbook" and link the runbook and rollback steps.
04:45 Avery: good. for launch gating, criteria are: stable p95 within 10% of baseline for 24h on canary, no sustained eviction spikes, and green on regression tests.
04:59 Priya: i'll signal QA sign-off only if the staged replay shows no eviction tail for two consecutive runs.
05:08 Ethan: also, i would like to add a small patch to the runtime that logs prefix-level eviction with sample keys — just enough to see the hot keys without PII. will add PR.
05:20 Marcus: perfect, that'll help root cause.
05:26 Riley: draft timeline — Wednesday test, follow-up Friday if green, then potential canary re-open next week.
05:34 Avery: okay let's call out owners again.
05:38 Marcus: Marcus -> runbook + eviction threshold config proposal; due 2026-05-05.
05:45 Ethan: Ethan -> instrumentation PR + per-shard eviction metric; due 2026-05-04.
05:51 Priya: Priya -> tests added + nightly; due 2026-05-07.
05:57 Riley: Riley -> rollback runbook + comms to on-call; due 2026-05-01.
06:03 Avery: i will consolidate into the launch readiness doc and share the deck and results after the Wednesday replay. thanks everyone.
